content.key_idea: LMT performance issues split almost evenly between hardware and application-level root causes, and only 29.6% can be diagnosed by existing online monitors, motivating EROICA's finer-grained online profiling.

encoding.color_means: green = identified/high-level categories, yellow = granular issue subtypes and offline-diagnosed cases, pink/salmon = unknown or undiagnosed cases

reusable_patterns: three-column categorical breakdown with percentages and consistent color coding across columns

summary: This motivation figure breaks down all large-model-training (LMT) performance issues observed in the authors' production GPU cluster (~100,000 GPUs) over nine months. It is drawn as a three-column categorical chart: the Type column splits issues into Hardware (44.4%), Application-level (48.2%), and Unknown (7.4%); the Issues column further breaks these into GPU, network, and other hardware problems, plus configuration and user-code problems; and the Diagnosis column shows that only 29.6% of issues could be identified online, while 63.0% required offline experiments and 7.4% went undiagnosed. Boxes are flat-filled in green, yellow, or pink/salmon to signal whether a category is high-level/identified, a granular subtype, or unknown/undiagnosed, with no arrows connecting the columns. The figure motivates EROICA's need for finer-grained, on-demand online profiling since most issues currently escape existing monitors.
summary_zh: 该图展示生产集群中大模型训练性能问题的三栏分类统计：类型（硬件 44.4%、应用层 48.2%、未知 7.4%）、细分问题及诊断结果（仅 29.6% 可在线定位，63.0% 需离线实验，7.4% 无法诊断），以此论证 EROICA 在线细粒度诊断的必要性。
